name: slider
behavior: APG slider pattern: each thumb is role=slider with aria-valuemin/aria-valuemax/aria-valuenow (and aria-valuetext when the number is not self-explanatory), aria-orientation, and an accessible name. ArrowRight/ArrowUp increment and ArrowLeft/ArrowDown decrement by one step, PageUp/PageDown by a larger step, Home/End jump to min/max. Multi-thumb range sliders follow APG slider (multi-thumb): every thumb is its own role=slider, each separately tabbable, and thumbs may not cross.

parts.note: the interactive band; its height reserves room for the thumb and the focus ring
the filled portion — from min to the thumb, or between two thumbs on a range slider

parts.statesNote: dragging raises to elevation-overlay per states.md; the hit target is padded to target-min even though the painted thumb is smaller

parts.note: tick on the track at each step/marked value
min/max labels flanking the track (Salt SliderTrack minLabel/maxLabel)
the live value shown at the thumb while dragging (Salt SliderTooltip); redundant to a screen reader — always aria-hidden

anatomyNotes: Intersection of shadcn Slider (Radix Root/Track/Range/Thumb) and Salt Slider/RangeSlider (track wrapper, ticks, mark labels, min/max labels, value tooltip). The four required parts are common; Salt's ticks/labels/tooltip are the optional parts above — they are anatomy (extra elements), not recipe, which is why shadcn simply omits them. Salt renders a hidden native range input inside each thumb for form participation: an implementation detail of the thumb part, not a part. Salt's restrictToMarks and format props are behavior options, never theme differences.
